implementation_notes: Task.WhenAll creates a task that completes when all of the supplied tasks have completed, so the fan-out is parts.Select(RouteAsync), the barrier is the await, and the aggregate is a fold over the returned Task<TResult>[] - the array index replaces the explicit correlation key. The routing branch lives inside RouteAsync (or a switch expression in the projection); the classic Aggregator object only earns its keep once parts cross a process or broker boundary, where a durable correlation store replaces the in-memory array.
code_sketch:
var results = await Task.WhenAll(parts.Select(RouteAsync));   // fan-out + barrier
return results.Aggregate(OrderReport.Empty, (acc, r) => acc.Merge(r));
pitfalls: Task.WhenAll surfaces only the first fault through the await; when a partial aggregate matters, inspect each task's Exception / use await Task.WhenAll inside a try-catch that reads all faulted tasks.
A part that never completes keeps the composite pending forever: attach a CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter deadline and let the aggregate see a partial result.
Passing a lazy or re-enumerated projection into WhenAll starts tasks you did not intend; materialise it (ToList) when the projection has side effects.

variants.name: TPL Dataflow network (per-kind blocks, batch/join aggregation)
variants.idiom_name: System.Threading.Tasks.Dataflow TransformBlock per part kind + BatchBlock/JoinBlock
variants.implementation_notes: The TPL Dataflow library is the in-process graph form: a TransformBlock (or ActionBlock) per part kind implements the processors, LinkTo with a predicate implements the routing, and an aggregation block - BatchBlock, JoinBlock or a custom block keyed by correlation id - together with the block's Completion task replaces the hand-written completion counter. Choose it when parts stream continuously or when per-stage parallelism and bounded capacity must be explicit; the library is part of .NET 6+ and a NuGet package for older targets.
pitfalls: Every block must be completed (Complete()) or its Completion task never finishes and the aggregate hangs.
With a bounded capacity, Post returns false instead of waiting; use SendAsync and observe the returned task, or parts are silently dropped.
Filtered links must not drop messages that no target accepts, or the source deadlocks offering them - the library documentation warns explicitly about this.
